Task 1: Querying an API and a Tidy-Style Function
Use GET() from the httr package to return information about a topic in the news.

getresult <- GET("https://newsapi.org/v2/everything?q=Dolly%20Parton&from=2026-09-01&language=en&pageSize=50&apiKey=2c43d850c570494389b660ffaf1757db")

Parse what is returned.

parsedresult <- fromJSON(rawToChar(getresult$content))
newsdata <- as_tibble(parsedresult$articles)

Write a function that allows the user to query this API.

querynews <- function(subject, time, key){
  
  getresult <- GET(paste0("https://newsapi.org/v2/everything?q=", 
                          gsub(" ", "%20", subject), 
                          "&from=", 
                          time, 
                          "&language=en&pageSize=50&apiKey=", 
                          key))
  
  parsedresult <- fromJSON(rawToChar(getresult$content))
  return(as_tibble(parsedresult$articles))
}

Task 2: Summarizing Roller Coaster Data
Read in roller coaster data and convert variables to factors as needed.

rollercoasters <- read_csv("http://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/online/datasets/635USrollercoasters.csv")

Rows: 635 Columns: 21

Delimiter: ","
chr (12): Coaster, Park, City, State, Census Region, AgeGroup, Scale, Type, ...
dbl  (9): Year Opened, TopSpeed, MaxHeight, Drop, Length, Duration, # of Inv...

ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.

rollercoasters <- rollercoasters |>
  mutate(AgeGroup = as.factor(AgeGroup),
         Scale = as.factor(Scale),
         Type = as.factor(Type),
         Design = as.factor(Design),
        `Inversions?` = as.factor(`Inversions?`))

Next, we will create a table showing counts between AgeGroup and Scale, limited to when Type is “Wood”. We will do this using two different methods:

Conditional two-way table using table(), by sub-setting the data first:


filtered <- filter(rollercoasters, Type == "Wood")

table(filtered$AgeGroup,
      filtered$Scale,
      useNA = "always")

  2:Recent      23      3      0      9    0

Stacked bar graph:

stackedbar <- ggplot(data = rollercoasters, aes(x=Scale, fill=AgeGroup))
stackedbar + geom_bar() +
   labs(x = "Scale", 
        y = "Number of Roller Coasters", 
        fill = "Age Group", 
        title = "Roller Coasters by Scale and Age Group")








Side-by-side bar graph:

sidebysidebar <- ggplot(data = rollercoasters, aes(x=Scale, fill=AgeGroup))
sidebysidebar + geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
   labs(x = "Scale", 
        y = "Number of Roller Coasters", 
        fill = "Age Group", 
        title = "Roller Coasters by Scale and Age Group")
